steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line cups with paper liners.
Mix flour, sugar, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a large bowl until well combined; stir in carrots, apple, raisins, walnuts, and coconut until evenly distributed.
Beat oil, eggs, and vanilla together in a separate bowl until well blended.
Stir egg mixture into carrot mixture until just moistened.
Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until the tops spring back when lightly pressed, about 20 minutes. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Morning Glory Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These morning glory muffins are made with a combination of carrots, apple, raisins, coconut, walnuts, and cinnamon. A glorious way to start any day.

video.description: Make any morning a special occasion with this Easy Morning Glory Muffins recipe. Combining apples, carrots, raisins, nuts, and coconut, this delicious breakfast muffin packs in a wide variety of fruits and vegetables. This video walks through each step of the process, starting with prepping your dry ingredients, followed by the wet ingredients, and then blending them together to make a colorful batter. Bake in a 350 degree oven and after 20 minutes, you’ll have an impressive batch of muffins in under one hour.

review.reviewBody: FYI... You can make these a lot healthier by replacing the oil with APPLESAUCE and using all whole wheat flour. Some recipes work with these subsitutions, some don't... but my friend made the healthy version of these for me, and I couldn't stop eating them!!! (so in the end, the nutritional value was probably the same since I was a muffin hog, but you get the point) TASTY!!!

Turned out great. Made mini-muffins (prefer less cakey). With my changes, not too sweet. The ingredients listed here perfectly balanced flavors - nothing overpowered. Baked 12 minutes at 400 (oopsie) on bottom shelf and then 2 more minutes after resetting to 350 on top shelf. 
Modifications:
For the white sugar, sub: 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, a tablespoon each of honey and molasses, beat into egg mixture
For white flour: used 1 cup white flour, 1/2 c whole wheat flour, 1/4 c flax meal, 1/4 c almond flour.
Coconut: Toasted about 3/4 c flaked coconut with 1/2 chopped walnuts in cast iron over low heat. 
Used olive oil.
Raisins: Soaked in hot water.

I modified this for dietary reasons using 1 cup of monk fruit sweetener in place of sugar, whole wheat pastry flour instead of all purpose and cut the oil down to 1/2 cup and added 1/4 cup melted butter. I also increased the salt to 1/2 tsp to help balance the sweetness. I also pre soak the raisins in hot water for about an hour before adding them (drained) to the mix. This keeps the muffins more moist when storing. I cook for a diabetic and he absolutely loves these muffins!

I used coconut oil instead of veg oil. Other than that I made them as written. It made a lot of batter for 12 muffins but the batter is stiff enough to overfill the 12. I had to bake them about 5 mins longer because of their size. They came out perfect, so moist. The overfilling made that nice muffin top that spills over the edge a little.... a little tricky to get out of the tin becauseof that, I had to wait until they completely cooled. Paper liners would make it easier. I used a honey crisp apple, though it might be too wet but I think it gave them the right amount of moisture. Nice golden color too.

Our favourites with a few modifications. Less sugar 3/4 cup (sometimes brown sugar); less oil (2/3 cup) added 1/2 cup each of unsalted sunflower seeds and pepita seeds. Also have to bake about 5-10 minutes longer. Paul

Pretty good recipe, except A cup of oil did seem too much. I used a cup of butter. Next time I will use 1/2 cup butter. I added 1/2 cup flour and 1 1/2 tsp of baking powder. I used a cup of zucchini (sqeezed water out), 10 ounces ounces of carrots. I forgot to add nuts, but they came out fine regardless. I used 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown. Made over 18 muffins.

Yummy!! I switched out the flour for a GF flour and I used 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce and 1/2 cup oil instead of the full cup of oil. They turned out perfectly, but i did have to cook them a bit longer. Probably 25 mins. My eggs were large, my apple was large... so I got 16 muffins.

These are really good!! I reduced the sugar to 1 cup and added one teaspoon of clove and nutmeg. Delicious. I did have to cook them a little longer - maybe 28 minutes. Next time I will try replacing some of the oil with applesauce. They are pretty greasy, but REALLY yummy!!

This is a delicious , dense muffin. Don't expect a fluffy muffin top, it doesn't rise much. I stuck pretty close to the recipe, making only 5 changes. First, I doubled the batch. Second, I used some brown sugar to replace some of the granulated (1 1/2 cups granulated, 1 cup brown), Third, I used a spice mixture similar to apple or pumpkin pie spice - I just like it better than plain cinnamon. It is mostly cinnamon, but also includes ginger, nutmeg, allspice, cloves and mace. Fourth, I used rehydrated, freeze dried carrots. This was a life saver when it came to prep for the carrots, all I had to do was boil water and add the dried carrots, instead of peeling, grating, etc. If I'd had freeze dried apples I would have used them as well. I obviously haven't tried this recipe with fresh carrots, but I don't think it would make any difference in flavor. And finally, I replaced 1/4 of the flour with unflavored protein powder. I'm thrilled with the results and expect that I will make this recipe again and again.

We used Pamela’s gluten free mix, and I don’t think I had enough carrots but wow these turned out awesome!!!! Made 20 (flat) muffins. Added pumpkin seeds to the tops which added nice touch. Will make these again!

These comments never cease to amaze me. It's like, I LOVE this recipe but I changed everything about it and added an additional 10 ingredients and cooked it 15 minutes longer. Other than that, it's great....Just stop. 

This was a pretty bad recipe. An entire cup of oil? Any real cook would have caught that sooner. You need a 1/2 cup of oil and 1/2 cup of applesauce. In addition, you need some spices, so it's not completely bland like this recipe. I added nutmeg, cloves, ginger, and cinnamon. And yes, they take waaaaay longer to bake than was posted. At least an additional 10 minutes.
So simple to make. I just omit the coconut as my family are not fans of it. They freeze great. 👍
Delicious. I added extra unsweetened applesauce, and sweetened coconut. My next try will be cranberries instead of raisins.

The first time I tried this morning glory muffin at a senior living homes deli, I tried one and instantly, I loved it, so I bought more to bring it home, I haven’t tried making it on my own but I keep buying it at the deli usually 6 muffins saving some for the seniors and they’re easily gone❤️❤️❤️

My kids love these too! I have made them vegan (flax instead of eggs) and they don't know! Love love love these as they are but they are very versatile and can add whatever is your taste. Try it out!!
I used craisins and pepitas but only because I was out of raisins and walnuts. I also used albertsons brand gluten-free flour. These are to die for! This is my favorite muffin recipe now!
Very moist
Moist and delicious! ❤️ Thank You for sharing
Great flavor! Came ot perfect!!

Substituted the following: -The sugar for 3/4 cup Splenda -I did not peel the apple -Walnuts for pecans -1/2 cup oil and 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce -halved the vanilla and cinnamon -topped with pumpkin seeds before baking
